name: John Fothergill
bio: Architect-trained aesthete, art dealer and later celebrated innkeeper; per Sox the one member of E. P. Warren's Lewes House brotherhood to become well known in Britain. Born 27 February 1876, son of George Fothergill of a fairly well-off Westmorland family; met Wilde at 19 through Robbie Ross and Reggie Turner, put in brief stints at the London School of Architecture (a pupil of architecture at 30 Manchester Street, 'to be near Sir Arthur Blomfield') and the Slade School of Art, dabbled in classical archaeology, and managed the Carfax Gallery. Wilde inscribed Fothergill's copy of The Ballad of Reading Gaol 'To Rowland Fothergill, the Architect of the Moon'. Ran the Spreadeagle at Thame near Oxford as innkeeper-author - the innkeeping diaries published in the 1930s and 1940s made his name - and died in a modest terraced house in Rugby on 26 April 1957, aged 81.
bio_note: All facts from Sox (1991): introduction pp. vii-viii (died at Rugby 26 April 1957, aged 81; archaeology, stints at the London School of Architecture and the Slade, the Carfax Gallery; 'the one member of the Lewes House brotherhood to become well known in Britain'); p. 133 (born 27 February 1876, son of George Fothergill of a 'fairly well-off Westmorland family'; full name John Rowland; the innkeeping diaries); p. 137 (met Wilde at 19 through Ross and Reggie Turner); p. 138 (architecture pupil at 30 Manchester Street; the Ballad inscription). Sox's caveat (p. 133): the memoir of 1954 is unfinished, 'highly disorganized', with 'few dates given'. On the Warren bond Sox says only that Fothergill 'taken up with Warren in Rome' (p. 142); no explicit romantic or sexual characterization appears.
